libs.note: BH-9289: the epic pass. A Blocked-by target outside the ai-build list that is not a decompose parent may be a hand-written epic. When every child (search for "Part of #N" and "epic #N", plus the sub-issues API) is closed, eb_pass posts one close question on the epic and one alert; with no human reply in EPIC_BLOCKER_DEFAULT_H it writes state/epic-blocker/<project>/<N>.met and bin/unblocked-children.sh treats the blocker as met. Runs inside bin/decompose-parent-close.sh after its close loop. Resolved once per process with lib_env_apply epic-blocker in a subshell; docs/notes/2026-11-09-BH-9289-epic-blocker.md.

knobs.note: The kill switch. 0 = off: no epic read, no question, no alert, and eb_met_list prints nothing, so no dependent is released by default. Read as ${EPIC_BLOCKER:-1}.
How long after the close question on a hand-written epic the pass waits for a reply before its dependents treat Blocked-by #N as met. A non-number or 0 reads as the fallback 24.
How many candidate epics one pass looks up (5 REST reads each, 2 of them search). The list rotates after state/epic-blocker/<project>/cursor. A non-number or 0 reads as the fallback 5.

The most comments one pass reads from an epic's thread (gh_rest_issue_comments max). A thread longer than this is a short read: the pass gives no verdict for that epic (SKIP), so it never asks twice or judges a reply it did not see. A non-number or 0 reads as the fallback 200.
